clue.text: Live in an artist's studio

definitions.meaning: a live broadcast is one going out as it happens
a painter working en plein air has the open sky for a studio

explanation.surface: Someone lives and works in a painter's studio.
explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: the second is cryptic, playing on painters who work outdoors, en plein air, so their studio is the open sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme being broadcast as it happens is said to be going out live on radio or television.

clue.text: One experiencing a similar calling

parts.note: calling is read not as a vocation but as what a person is called, their name

explanation.surface: Someone who feels the same vocation as another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a name with another person has, in a punning sense, the same calling.

clue.text: Left in anger, hurt about loud hint one's unfit to go there

definitions.text: hint one's unfit to go there

indicators.note: the word Left is placed inside the word for anger

parts.note: heat is passion or anger

indicators.note: the word for hurt goes around the letter for loud

parts.note: to hurt is to harm
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone storms off angry and wounded after a heavy hint that they are out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hint' belongs with the definition: the hint is that you are unfit, so you should go there.
explanation.definitionFit: A health farm is a residential retreat for people wanting to get fit, so a hint you are unfit suggests you go there.

clue.text: Batting in last Oval match for this team

indicators.note: batting means hitting about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket side bats in the final match at the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, which makes 'Batting' read as cricket; ASTON VILLA is in fact a Birmingham football club, found by rearranging IN LAST OVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English football club, an example of a team.

clue.text: Did he fetch tobacco and mostly real ale to be consumed?

indicators.note: the ale is drunk, taken inside the shortened word
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: real and right are both intensifiers, as in a real or right mess
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether some explorer brought back tobacco and real ale to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'real' is the intensifier, as in a real or right mess. Sir Walter Raleigh is credited with popularising tobacco in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh, the Elizabethan adventurer, is traditionally said to have brought tobacco to England.

clue.text: End objections raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Objections are raised to bring something to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short end left of a cigarette or pencil.

clue.text: Very reliable pet food

parts.note: a hot tip is one that is very reliable
a dog is a common pet

explanation.surface: Food for a pet that can be depended upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage in a bread roll, a kind of food.

clue.text: Woman to help mum turns out, getting little cuddle

indicators.note: the word for little holds the other letters in its embrace

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of turns are put out of order

explanation.surface: A woman turns out to help a mother, and gets a small hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman to help mum' is the definition: the woman nurses another mother's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse is a woman employed to breastfeed another mother's baby.

clue.text: One ruminating before accepting E European's comeback

indicators.note: the word for before takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: a comeback turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a Pole is an East European

explanation.surface: Someone thinking things over before welcoming back an East European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E European' is a Pole, an East European, not just the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes chew the cud, so one is literally a ruminating animal.

clue.text: Zoe doesn't have quite such a dotty appearance

definitions.text: Zoe doesn't have quite such a dotty appearance

parts.words: Zoe doesn't have quite such a dotty appearance
parts.note: the two dots over the e in Zoë look like the German sign but are strictly a diaeresis, marking a separate vowel

explanation.surface: A woman called Zoe is not quite as scatterbrained as some.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has Zoë with two dots on the e; those dots are a diaeresis, which looks the same as the German vowel mark but is not quite it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of dots placed over a German vowel such as ü is that mark.

clue.text: Word put in for us — study appears to demand too much work

indicators.note: the word for Word is put inside the word for us

parts.note: our means belonging to us
a verb is a part of speech, a doing word
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A word is slipped in on our behalf: the course seems to ask too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To overburden is to load someone with more work than they can bear.

clue.text: Used to be hard to wake

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It used to be difficult to rouse someone from sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake' is not rousing from sleep but the trail behind a moving boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The wash of a ship is the disturbed water it leaves behind, its wake.

clue.text: Change tack about food, say, getting round to this?

definitions.text: Change tack about food, say, getting round to this?

indicators.note: the word for changing tack goes around the rest

parts.note: to veer is to change direction or tack

indicators.note: getting round means the joined pieces are turned to read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Someone changes their diet and comes round to eating this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a convert to vegetarian food coming round to eating this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone changing tack about food, turning vegetarian, might well come round to eating a meatless burger.

clue.text: Strike follows more undisguised nonsense

indicators.note: the word for strike comes after the other piece

parts.note: balder means plainer or more bare
to dash is to strike or smash

explanation.surface: A strike follows even plainer nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is a synonym for senseless talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Listening, studied female's call — it's misleading

indicators.note: listening means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: read, past tense, means studied, as at university
her means belonging to a female
to ring is to telephone or call

explanation.surface: A listener hears a woman's call and finds it deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a false clue or distraction, something misleading.

clue.text: Not paying for basic computer programming

definitions.meaning: a failure to pay a debt
the standard setting a program uses unless told otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone skips payment for an introductory computing course.
explanation.definitionFit: A default is a failure to pay a debt, and also the preset option in software.

clue.text: Tirade from girl vexed about tease

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the word for vexed goes around the word for tease

parts.note: ate means worried or vexed, as in what's eating you
to rib is to tease

explanation.surface: A girl is annoyed at being teased and lets fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade.

clue.text: If it's returned, for instance, woman harbouring desire finally gets embraced

definitions.text: If it's returned, for instance, woman harbouring desire finally gets embraced

indicators.note: the woman with her letter is held inside the other piece
returned means the abbreviation is turned to read backwards

parts.note: eg is short for for example

indicators.note: the word for woman holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: the last letter of desire

explanation.surface: A flirtatious look, if answered, leads to a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes such a look's effect: returned, it leads to an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: The glad eye is an amorous look; returned, it may well lead to an embrace.

clue.text: Outsiders going by a tag hanging to identify this sword

indicators.note: the outer letters of the phrase are dropped, leaving the inner run

explanation.surface: A tag hangs on a sword to identify it.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of BY A TAG HANGING and the rest gives the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A yataghan is a Turkish sword with a curved blade and no guard.

clue.text: Work on total needed to capture very large marsupial

indicators.note: the joined pieces hold the other letters inside
in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a sum is a total
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Work needs a big figure to catch a huge pouched animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is an American marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Obviously, a man can have one by the throat

definitions.text: Obviously, a man can have one by the throat

parts.words: Obviously, a man can have one by the throat
parts.note: the first man, by name, would naturally own the lump in a man's neck; by the throat sounds like grabbing someone

explanation.surface: A man can seize someone by the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulge of the larynx at the front of a man's neck is named after the first man.

clue.text: One, quivered, perhaps, when bowing

parts.note: quivered means carrying a quiver of arrows, and bowing means using a bow, not trembling and stooping

explanation.surface: Someone trembles as they bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots with a bow and carries arrows in a quiver.

clue.text: Acts like a typical consumer

parts.note: a consumer is read literally as one who consumes food

explanation.surface: Someone behaves like an ordinary shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to take it in, which is what a person does when having a meal.

clue.text: Was aware of firm's special designer clothing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters dress the abbreviation, holding it inside
special suggests something made differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a company's exclusive designer clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like part of the designer picture but signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recognised something is to have been aware of it or acknowledged it.

clue.text: Votes against any changes on spec, at first

indicators.note: changes means the letters of any are rearranged
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word spec, the start of the specification

explanation.surface: People vote down any changes to the specification at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Nays are votes against a motion, the opposite of ayes.

clue.text: Get out, or staying in?

definitions.meaning: to step down from a vehicle
a fire that has stayed in is still burning

explanation.surface: A question of whether to go out or stay at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying in' sounds like staying at home, but a fire that is in is still burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get off a bus or train; a fire still burning is alight.

clue.text: It's often said to follow involuntary expulsion

definitions.text: It's often said to follow involuntary expulsion

parts.words: It's often said to follow involuntary expulsion
parts.note: the involuntary expulsion is a sneeze, not someone thrown out of a club

explanation.surface: Something usually said after someone is thrown out against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: The customary words spoken to someone who has just sneezed.

clue.text: Something from the wood? A lot — a pig's drunk!

indicators.note: drunk means swallowed, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: many means a lot
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A tipsy remark about a pig wandering out of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as tipsy, but here it means swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hardwood timber, something that comes from trees in a wood.
